sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Gwendolyn Willow Wilson (born August 31, 1982) is an American comics writer, prose author, and essayist.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Her work is most often categorized as magical realism.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Wilson's prose works include the novels Alif the Unseen (2012), which won the 2013 World Fantasy Award for "Novel", and The Bird King (2019).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: She was one of the lead creators in the relaunch of the Ms. Marvel title for Marvel Comics and co-creator of its starring character Kamala Khan, a 16-year-old Muslim superhero.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Wilson was the writer on the Ms. Marvel series from February 2014 to February 2019; the first volume won the 2015 Hugo Award for "Best Graphic Story".

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: , Wilson has been the writer on the ongoing Poison Ivy series for DC Comics.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Her original comic series include the Invisible Kingdom (2019–2021) for Dark Horse Comics, which won the 2020 Eisner Award for "Best New Series", and The Hunger and the Dusk (2023–2026) for IDW Publishing, which was a finalist for the 2025 Hugo Award for "Best Graphic Story or Comic".

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Wilson was born on August 31, 1982, in Monmouth County, New Jersey, and grew up in Morganville.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Wilson lived in the county until she was 12.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: However, in an interview with Newsrama in 2013, she erroneously said she was born in Morris County and spent the first ten years of her life there.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Her parents were atheists who renounced Protestantism in the late 1960s, hence Wilson was not raised in a religious household.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Wilson first encountered comics when she read an anti-smoking pamphlet featuring the X-Men in the fifth grade.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: The characters fascinated her and she began watching the cartoon X-Men every Saturday.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Two years later she and her family moved to Boulder, Colorado, where Wilson continued to pursue her interest in comics and other forms of popular culture such as tabletop role-playing games.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: After high school, Wilson attended Boston University to pursue a degree in history.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: During her sophomore year, Wilson began experiencing adrenal problems and the associated discomfort resulted in her studying a number of religions, including Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: After studying Judaism she focused on Islam, which appealed to her because "to become a Muslim is sort of a deal between you and God."

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: The 9/11 terrorist attack set back her religious studies – fearing she had misjudged the religion – but she later resumed her studies.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: In 2003, shortly before her graduation, Wilson agreed to teach English in Cairo.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: During the plane journey, Wilson converted to Islam; stating she "made peace with God.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: I called him Allah."

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: According to Butterfly Mosque, upon arrival in Cairo, Wilson secretly practiced Islam.

sentences.section: Converting to Islam
sentences.text: After becoming engaged to an Egyptian, she began to practice it more openly.

sentences.section: Career
sentences.text: Wilson's writing career began from her work as a freelance music critic for DigBoston.

sentences.section: Career
sentences.text: After moving to Cairo, she contributed articles to the Atlantic Monthly, The New York Times Magazine, and the National Post.

sentences.section: Career
sentences.text: She was also a regular contributor to the now-defunct Egyptian opposition weekly Cairo Magazine.

sentences.section: Career
sentences.text: Wilson was the first Western journalist to be granted a private interview with Ali Gomaa after his promotion to the position of Grand Mufti of Egypt.

sentences.section: Career
sentences.text: Additionally, Wilson released a memoir titled The Butterfly Mosque about life in Egypt during the Mubarak regime, which was named a Seattle Times Best Book of 2010.

sentences.text: Her first graphic novel, Cairo, with art by M.K.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Perker, was published by Vertigo in 2007, and named one of the best graphic novels of 2007 by Publishers Weekly, The Edmonton Journal/CanWest News, and Comics Worth Reading.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: The paperback edition of Cairo was named one of Best Graphic Novels for High School Students in 2008 by School Library Journal, and one of 2009's Top Ten Graphic Novels for Teens by the American Library Association.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Her first ongoing comic series, Air, launched by Vertigo in 2008 reunited her with Perker, and was nominated for an Eisner Award for 'Best New Series' of 2009.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: NPR named Air one of the top comics of 2009, and it also received acclaim from the Fairfield Weekly, Comic Book Resources, Marie Claire, and Library Journal.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Other works for DC include fill-in issues #704 and 706 of Superman, the five-issue mini-series Vixen: Return of the Lion, starring the Justice League member Vixen with art by CAFU, and The Outsiders.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Wilson then wrote Mystic (2011), a four-issue miniseries for Marvel Comics with art by David Lopez.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Although a CrossGen revival, Willow's Mystic bears little resemblance to its previous incarnation.

sentences.section: Cairo, Air, and Alif the Unseen (2007–2013)
sentences.text: Her debut novel Alif the Unseen (Grove/Atlantic) won the 2013 World Fantasy Award for best novel.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: In 2014, Marvel debuted a new Ms. Marvel series written by Wilson.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Wilson had already had a few forays into the comic book industry, having worked on titles such as Superman and Vixen previously.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: She received an email for an interview with David Gabriel, a senior vice-president at Marvel Entertainment.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: By that point Wilson was almost finished with her second novel, but she took the time to speak with him.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Shortly thereafter she was offered the opportunity to co-create a new version of Ms. Marvel named Kamala Khan alongside Sana Amanat, a director and editor at Marvel Entertainment.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: The process of crafting Kamala was detailed; both artists wished to create a teenage Muslim American girl.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Before settling on her Pakistani heritage the two debated the idea of making her a Somali American girl.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: While creating Kamala as a character the duo expected negativity, not just from people who were anti-Muslim, but also from Muslims who believed Kamala should be portrayed in a certain way.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: The crafting also focused on smaller details: Wilson did not believe Kamala should wear a hijab due to a majority of teenage Muslim American girls not wearing them.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Despite their initial fears, Kamala was received positively.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Some sources described her as easy to relate to, even likening her to a modern-day Peter Parker.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Others even viewed Kamala as a symbol for equality and representation among different religions.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Wilson was then brought on to write the 4 issue "The Burning World" arc for the fourth volume of the ongoing X-Men series in 2015; Wilson was the "first female writer to work on X-Men" since the relaunch "with an all-female X-Men roster".

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Marvel then cancelled its entire publishing line, including both Ms. Marvel and X-Men, for the Secret Wars (2015) event storyline.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: X-Men was not continued during the post-Secret Wars publishing initiative All-New, All-Different Marvel.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: In May 2015, Marvel launched the limited series A-Force as part of the Secret Wars (2015) event storyline.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: The series, co-written by Wilson and Marguerite Bennett and drawn by Jorge Molina, features Marvel's first all-female team of Avengers.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: In 2016, Wilson returned as co-writer, this time with Kelly Thompson, for the first arc of the second volume of A-Force as part of Marvel's All-New, All-Different Marvel initiative.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: A second volume of Ms. Marvel, starring Kamala and written by Wilson, also debuted as part of Marvel's All-New, All-Different Marvel initiative.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Ms. Marvel #31—the 50th issue of Ms. Marvel featuring Kamala—was published in June 2018.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: To mark the occasion, Marvel brought in additional collaborators for the issue: writers Saladin Ahmed, Rainbow Rowell, and Hasan Minhaj, and artists Nico Leon, Bob Quinn, Gustavo Duarte, and Elmo Bondoc.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: Wilson finished writing the series with issue #38 in February 2019.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: In November 2018, Wilson began writing Wonder Woman from DC Comics with issue #58.

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: The character battles Ares in an arc entitled "The Just War."

sentences.section: Kamala Khan, A-Force and Wonder Woman (2014–2019)
sentences.text: In August 2019, Wilson announced that she was leaving the series; her final issue was #81 in October 2019.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Wilson's fantasy novel The Bird King was released in March 2019 by Grove Press.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The story concerns the flight of Fatima and Hassan, a concubine and mapmaker, respectively, from service to the Emirate of Granada's last sultan.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Also in March 2019, Wilson and artist Christian Ward debuted a new creator-owned series titled Invisible Kingdom which was published by Dark Horse's Berger Books imprint.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: It won the 2020 Eisner Award for Best New Series; Wilson was nominated for Best Writer for her work on both the Invisible Kingdom and Ms. Marvel.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The first ten issues were released as individual issues.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Invisible Kingdom switched to an original graphic novel format to finish the series.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Academic David Higgins, in 2020 for the Journal of the Fantastic in the Arts, wrote that "Wilson is one of the preeminent fantastic creators of our contemporary moment", noting that she "is a skilled, accomplished, and award-winning author".

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: In 2020, Wilson wrote the final two issues of The Dreaming from DC Comics, with art by Nick Robles; the series is part of The Sandman Universe.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Wilson and Robles then created the 12-issue limited series The Dreaming: Waking Hours.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: A miniseries starring Poison Ivy was announced by DC Comics in March 2022 as part of the publisher's "Pride Month" initiative.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Poison Ivy was originally intended to be a six-issue miniseries written by Wilson with art by Marcio Takara.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The first issue was published in June 2022, with subsequent issues published monthly.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: In August 2022, DC Comics announced that the miniseries would be extended by an additional six issues, with Atagun Ilhan joining Takara in illustrating the second arc.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: In February 2023, DC Comics announced that the miniseries would be further expanded into an ongoing series.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: In April 2023, IDW announced Wilson and artist Chris Wildgoose as the creators of a new original ongoing series titled The Hunger and the Dusk.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Six issues were released between July 2023 and February 2024.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The first book of The Hunger and the Dusk was a 2025 Hugo Award finalist for Best Graphic Story or Comic.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The Hunger and the Dusk: Book Two began in July 2024.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: However, in January 2025, IDW announced that "due to unforeseen delays in the book's production", issues #4–6 were canceled as individual print comics and would instead be released in the trade paperback collection for the second book.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: This collection was released in July 2026; issues #4–6 also received individual digital releases.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: In 2025, Wilson became the writer for the new ongoing Black Cat series for Marvel Comics, with art by Gleb Melnikov.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: She contributed a backup story featuring Static and Ms. Marvel in Batman/Deadpool #1 for DC Comics.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Also in 2025, Wilson reunited with artist M.K.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Perker to write the graphic novel The Stoneshore Register for Berger Books.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: Starting in May 2027, Wilson will write the new Captain Marvel ongoing series featuring Carol Danvers with Rachael Stott on art duties.

sentences.section: The Bird King, Invisible Kingdom and Poison Ivy (2019–present)
sentences.text: The comic is set after the Avengers: Armageddon crossover event.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: Since 2007, Wilson has lived in Seattle with her husband, Omar.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: She has two daughters.
